reasoning: The core problem — whether cross-examination (targeted follow-up questions forcing a model to commit to sub-claims, surfacing self-contradiction) detects errors in multi-step reasoning — is directly addressed by Cohen et al.'s "LM vs LM: Detecting Factual Errors via Cross Examination" (EMNLP 2023), which has an examiner LM issue multi-turn follow-up questions to reveal inconsistencies implying errors at ~0.8 recall/precision. The AI-safety debate literature (Barnes & Christiano's debate writeup and the obfuscated-arguments work) formalizes the exact mechanism of cross-examination forcing commitment-or-contradiction, and error-localization-in-reasoning-chains with planted errors is covered by "FindTheFlaws" (2503.22989) and "Towards Scalable Oversight with Collaborative Multi-Agent Debate in Error Detection" (2510.20963); baseline-judge-vs-interaction comparisons appear in "On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs" and inference-only debate experiments. The specific narrow packaging (small open model, exactly-one-planted-error synthetic chains, cheap 2-3 prompted follow-ups measured for localization rate vs a no-interaction baseline) is a minor unexplored configuration rather than a new problem, so gaps are minor.

evidence.title: LM vs LM: Detecting Factual Errors via Cross Examination
evidence.summary: An examiner LM issues multi-turn follow-up questions to an examinee LM to surface inconsistencies that imply factual errors, achieving ~0.75-0.84 recall and ~0.82-0.87 precision. Directly implements the proposal's central mechanism of targeted cross-examination questions revealing self-contradiction.

evidence.title: Writeup: Progress on AI Safety via Debate (and Debate update: Obfuscated arguments problem)
evidence.summary: Formalizes cross-examination as forcing a debater to either commit to all sub-claims (so the flaw can be localized) or answer inconsistently (so the contradiction is exhibited to the judge). This is exactly the proposal's framing of follow-up questions forcing commitment to break obfuscation.

evidence.title: FindTheFlaws: Annotated Errors for Detecting Flawed Reasoning and Scalable Oversight Research
evidence.summary: Provides annotated reasoning chains with located errors for studying judge/debate-based error detection and localization, covering the proposal's planted-error localization measurement on multi-step arguments.

evidence.title: Towards Scalable Oversight with Collaborative Multi-Agent Debate in Error Detection
evidence.summary: Studies multi-agent debate for detecting/localizing errors in reasoning, comparing interactive protocols against single-judge baselines — the same baseline-vs-interaction comparison the proposal sets up.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
evidence.summary: Empirically compares judge accuracy under direct reading versus interactive debate/consultancy protocols with small judge models, the inference-only baseline-vs-interaction experimental design the proposal proposes.

evidence.title: Inference-Only Debate Experiments Using Math Problems
evidence.summary: Inference-only, prompting-based debate experiments on math reasoning measuring whether interaction improves judge accuracy/error detection — closely matches the proposal's compute-light inference-only setup.
